item.content:encoded: A goal from Mads Hansen in the ninth minute of stoppage time gave Brommapojkarna a sensational 6-5 victory over AIK in Sweden's Allsvenskan on Saturday as AIK came back from 5-1 down, only to lose with virtually the last kick of the game. After a goalless first half between the Stockholm sides, BP took the lead through Simon Strand in the 46th minute and Abdihakim Ali equalised before the game exploded into chaos, with BP netting four goals in 12 minutes to race into a 5-1 wlead ith 20 minutes to play. Incredibly, AIK came back with four unanswered goals of their own, Johan Hove netting in the seventh minute of stoppage time to make it 5-5, but Hansen scored from close range two minutes later to give BP their first league win over AIK at the 20th attempt. "It was value for money for those who came here today," a beaming Strand told broadcaster TV4. "It was a fun game up to 5-1, and then it was an uphill battle. But no, it was really fun, completely blown away after a match like this, to be honest," he added. AIK are ninth in the 16-team standings on 33 points, 21 points behind leaders Sirius. BP are 11th on 30 points.

item.title: Abbas adia eleições palestinas e marca pleito presidencial para setembro de 2027
item.description: O presidente palestino Mahmoud Abbas adiou neste sábado as eleições legislativas previstas para o próximo mês até 11 de setembro de 2027 e convocou uma eleição presidencial para a mesma data, atribuindo a culpa pelo adiamento a Israel e à situação de segurança nos territórios palestinos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente palestino Mahmoud Abbas adiou neste sábado as eleições legislativas previstas para o próximo mês até 11 de setembro de 2027 e convocou uma eleição presidencial para a mesma data, atribuindo a culpa pelo adiamento a Israel e à situação de segurança nos territórios palestinos. O decreto de Abbas citou “obstáculos impostos por medidas israelenses” e a necessidade de estabelecer condições políticas, de segurança e no terreno adequadas para “eleições livres, justas e inclusivas”, informou a agência oficial de notícias palestina WAFA. O decreto convocou os palestinos em Jerusalém, na Cisjordânia e em Gaza a votar. Havia sérias dúvidas de que a votação da Autoridade Palestina fosse ocorrer no mês que vem. Os palestinos não realizam eleições legislativas ou presidenciais desde 2005-06, período após o qual o rival de Abbas, o grupo islâmico Hamas, assumiu o controle de Gaza, destituindo seus partidários. Abbas tem governado por decreto desde que seu mandato presidencial expirou em 2009. A Autoridade Palestina realizou eleições municipais em abril na Cisjordânia e em Deir al-Balah, no centro de Gaza, a única cidade do enclave que participou. A votação foi a primeira eleição realizada em Gaza desde 2006. Segundo o decreto, os ataques militares israelenses, a expansão dos assentamentos, a violência dos colonos e as restrições de circulação na Cisjordânia, incluindo Jerusalém Oriental, juntamente com a retenção contínua por parte de Israel das receitas tributárias palestinas, criaram desafios para a preparação e a realização das eleições em novembro deste ano. Em Gaza, o decreto apontou para “condições excepcionais de segurança e humanitárias”, a retirada incompleta das forças israelenses, a falta de progresso na reconstrução e o fracasso na implementação de acordos para o envio de forças internacionais de estabilização e da polícia. As restrições israelenses ao acesso de funcionários da comissão eleitoral e observadores internacionais a Gaza e Jerusalém Oriental também complicaram os preparativos, segundo o decreto. Não houve comentário imediato de Israel sobre o anúncio de Abbas, com autoridades indisponíveis para comentar no sábado, o sabá judaico. Israel normalmente proíbe a Autoridade Palestina de realizar eleições em Jerusalém Oriental, território que conquistou na guerra de 1967 e posteriormente anexou, em uma medida que a maioria dos países não reconhece.

item.title: French prodigy Seixas wins Giro di Lombardia, his first Monument
item.description: French prodigy Paul Seixas rode solo to claim the first Monument victory of his career at the Giro di Lombardia on Saturday, ahead of Spain's Enric Mas and Italy's Giulio Ciccone.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: French prodigy Paul Seixas rode solo to claim the first Monument victory of his career at the Giro di Lombardia on Saturday, ahead of Spain's Enric Mas and Italy's Giulio Ciccone. The 20-year-old attacked 19 km from the finish in Como (Italy) to claim the title won by Tadej Pogacar for the last five years. The Slovenian missed the race after crashing at the Vuelta a Espana two months ago. Seixas won his first Monument — one of the five most prestigious one-day races in professional cycling — in his third appearance. He finished seventh in this race last year and second behind Pogacar at the last Liege–Bastogne–Liege. "It's crazy, it feels like a dream," Seixas said. "Everything went perfect. I had amazing legs, I had the feeling that today was a great day and I managed to make the difference at the moment I choose." Seixas, who finished fourth in this year's Tour de France, pulled clear on the Civiglio climb with 19 km to go. Britain's Tom Pidcock and Ciccone were the only riders able to follow his wheel. The Frenchman dropped both rivals a few hundred metres later and rode alone over the final 18 km to become the youngest Monument winner since 1944 and youngest ever winner of the Giro di Lombardia. SEIXAS ENDS FRENCH WAIT The Decathlon–CMA CGM rider is the first Frenchman to win a Monument since Julian Alaphilippe at Milan–San Remo in 2019, and the first to triumph at the Giro di Lombardia since Thibaut Pinot in 2018. The victory came two weeks after a huge disappointment for Seixas at the World Championships, where he finished 15th after starting among the favourites. "After the championship, I moved on to other things; I trained hard to get here," Seixas said. "It’s incredible." The 239 km ride from Bergamo to Como began with a [USN:L6N45W026 TEXT:"five-minute protest"] in the peloton to highlight growing safety concerns following a series of incidents involving race vehicles. After organisers completed the start countdown, the peloton remained stationary, before double Olympic champion Remco Evenepoel stepped forward to explain the riders' action. The protest came days after riders Thomas Gloag and Marcel Camprubi were struck by a police motorcycle during Tre Valli Varesine. Britain's Finlay Tarling was killed in a collision with a vehicle during the Tour of Portugal in August.

item.title: Cyclisme-Seixas remporte le Tour de Lombardie, son premier monument
item.description: Paul Seixas (Decathlon-CMA CGM) a remporté samedi le premier monument du cyclisme de sa jeune carrière en triomphant sur le Tour de Lombardie, dont il est devenu le plus jeune vainqueur de l'histoire devant l'Espagnol Enric Mas (Movistar) et l'Italien Giulio Ciccone (Lidl-Trek).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Paul Seixas (Decathlon-CMA CGM) a remporté samedi le premier monument du cyclisme de sa jeune carrière en triomphant sur le Tour de Lombardie, dont il est devenu le plus jeune vainqueur de l'histoire devant l'Espagnol Enric Mas (Movistar) et l'Italien Giulio Ciccone (Lidl-Trek). Le Français de tout juste 20 ans succède au palmarès au Slovène Tadej Pogacar, quintuple vainqueur sortant et absent sur les bords du lac de Côme (Italie) après sa chute sur le dernier Tour d'Espagne. Le quatrième du dernier Tour de France est le premier Tricolore à lever les bras sur un monument - les cinq courses d'un jour les plus prestigieuses - depuis Julian Alaphilippe en 2019 sur Milan-San Remo et le premier à s'imposer sur le Tour de Lombardie depuis Thibaut Pinot en 2018. Paul Seixas devient également le plus jeune vainqueur d'un monument depuis 1944. "C'est fou, c'est comme dans un rêve", a-t-il réagi, incrédule. "Je ne réalise pas. Tout s'est déroulé parfaitement. J'avais des jambes incroyables et le sentiment qu'aujourd'hui était un grand jour. J'ai réussi à faire la différence au moment que j'avais choisi." Paul Seixas a une nouvelle fois démontré qu'il était l'un des coureurs les plus talentueux du peloton malgré son jeune âge. Il s'est imposé samedi dès sa troisième participation à un monument, après sa septième place ici-même l'an passé et sa deuxième place de Liège-Bastogne-Liège, en avril, derrière l'ogre Tadej Pogacar. En l'absence du double champion du monde, le coureur de l'équipe Decathlon-CMA CGM n'a pas loupé le coche. Il a accéléré dans l'ascension du Civiglio, à 19 km de l'arrivée. Seuls le Britannique Tom Pidcock et Giulio Ciccone ont d'abord réussi à prendre sa roue, avant de craquer quelques centaines de mètres plus loin. Paul Seixas a ainsi filé vers la victoire en solitaire, résistant à ses poursuivants pendant les 18 derniers kilomètres. Le vainqueur de La Flèche wallonne, en avril, a parfaitement rebondi après son immense déception des Mondiaux, où il avait terminé 15e deux semaines plus tôt malgré son statut de favori aux côtés de Remco Evenepoel ou d'Isaac del Toro. Le Belge et le Mexicain ont respectivement terminé quatrième et 28e samedi. "Après le championnat, je suis passé à autre chose, je me suis entraîné dur pour arriver ici", a expliqué Paul Seixas. "C'est incroyable."

item.title: Ataque russo mata 20 na Ucrânia um dia após Trump ter flexibilizado sanções contra Moscou sobre diesel
item.description: Vinte pessoas, incluindo três crianças, morreram em um ataque russo à cidade de Zaporizhzhia, no sul da Ucrânia, no sábado, um dia depois que o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, anunciou um acordo para suspender as sanções contra o diesel russo — um grande revés para Kiev.
item.dc:creator: Sergiy Chalyi, Max Hunder
item.content:encoded: Vinte pessoas, incluindo três crianças, morreram em um ataque russo à cidade de Zaporizhzhia, no sul da Ucrânia, no sábado, um dia depois que o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, anunciou um acordo para suspender as sanções contra o diesel russo — um grande revés para Kiev. Uma menina de seis anos estava entre as vítimas fatais quando um ataque reduziu parte de um prédio de apartamentos a escombros. Seu avô chorava ao lado do corpo dela, deitado no chão dentro de um saco branco, depois que as equipes de resgate o retiraram dos escombros. “Hoje, a Rússia agradeceu pelo levantamento das sanções às exportações de diesel lançando cinco bombas planadoras sobre prédios residenciais em Zaporizhzhia”, disse o presidente Volodymyr Zelenskiy, em uma de suas críticas mais contundentes até agora à Casa Branca. Outras 18 pessoas ficaram feridas no ataque a Zaporizhzhia, uma cidade industrial cujos arredores ficam a menos de 30 km da linha de frente. O bombardeio foi o mais recente de uma série de ataques que causaram um grande número de vítimas em toda a Ucrânia. Quase 80 civis foram mortos em ataques russos ao longo de dois dias nesta semana. “O aniversário dela seria no final do mês”, disse Anatoliy Chumniy, avô da menina de seis anos, entre lágrimas. O governador local, Mykhailo Semikin, disse que a Rússia atacou vários locais simultaneamente nas primeiras horas deste sábado. Equipes de resgate escalaram os escombros para retirar com vida outros moradores do prédio. Um homem, cuja perna estava presa nos escombros, gritava de dor enquanto era resgatado. Zaporizhzhia, com uma população pré-guerra de mais de 700 mil habitantes, tem sido alvo constante de bombardeios russos, com ataques que se intensificaram nos últimos meses. “A noite passada foi mais uma confirmação de que a Rússia interpreta qualquer diminuição da pressão como um sinal de que pode, supostamente, continuar lutando, de que pode, supostamente, continuar lançando bombas sobre as cidades. São necessários sinais diferentes”, declarou Zelenskiy. TRUMP SUSPENDE SANÇÕES AO DIESEL A decisão de Trump de suspender as sanções às exportações russas de diesel ocorre no momento em que seu governo busca conter os preços dos combustíveis, que subiram acentuadamente durante o conflito dos EUA com o Irã. Kiev, por sua vez, havia instado Washington a aumentar a pressão sobre Moscou, em um esforço para forçá-la a entrar em negociações sérias para pôr fim à guerra que já dura quatro anos e meio. Trump, por sua vez, criticou os ataques ucranianos a refinarias de petróleo russas, que, segundo ele, elevaram os preços globais. Kiev afirmou que deseja a suspensão total de todos os ataques a instalações energéticas por ambos os lados, enquanto Moscou ataca a rede elétrica da Ucrânia. No sábado, partes de Kiev e da região circundante ficaram sem energia elétrica, levando os trens do metrô da cidade a uma paralisação total pela segunda vez nesta semana. Os últimos ataques ocorreram depois que autoridades ucranianas e europeias mantiveram conversações com negociadores dos EUA em Miami na sexta-feira, com o objetivo de elaborar uma proposta comum para pôr fim à guerra, segundo uma pessoa a par das discussões. Trump anunciou o acordo sobre o diesel enquanto as negociações estavam em andamento, uma medida que, segundo Zelenskiy, pegou Kiev de surpresa. O presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, disse após uma ligação com Trump que era improvável uma retomada imediata das negociações de paz, citando ataques com drones ucranianos a Moscou. Quatro civis foram mortos e outros cinco ficaram feridos em consequência dos ataques ucranianos à região de Luhansk, controlada pela Rússia, no leste da Ucrânia, afirmou no sábado o governador nomeado pela Rússia. A Reuters não conseguiu verificar a informação de forma independente e não houve comentário imediato da Ucrânia.

item.title: Red Bull's Verstappen fastest in Singapore to claim 50th career pole
item.description: He repeated his heroics from the sprint qualifying session a day earlier.
item.dc:creator: Rohith Nair
item.content:encoded: Red Bull's Max Verstappen claimed the 50th pole position of his career when he went fastest in qualifying under the lights at the Singapore Grand Prix on Saturday, repeating his heroics from the sprint qualifying session a day earlier. Verstappen clocked one minute 31.373 seconds at the Marina Bay Street Circuit and will have Ferrari's Charles Leclerc alongside him on the front row, with the Monegasque driver just 0.054 seconds slower than the four-times champion. Leclerc's team mate Lewis Hamilton was third fastest and championship leader Kimi Antonelli was fourth quickest for Mercedes. "The margins are very close between us throughout all of qualifying, so of course, very happy to be on pole because this is the one that I wanted," Verstappen said ahead of his 250th race. "The car has been pretty strong all weekend. Of course, I always think that you can be better, but it was enough for pole, so very happy with that." Verstappen, who [USN:L1N45W02M TEXT:"won a chaotic sprint"] in wet conditions earlier on Saturday, topped the timesheets despite gearbox issues in Q2 to claim his second straight pole of the season. Leclerc had struggled in Q1 and Q2 but found his groove in Q3 to put Ferrari on the front row right at the end of the session. "I had some weird things going on with the brakes, car pulling a bit under braking, which is not so nice on a track like here," Leclerc said. "But then in Q3, the lap was okay. I did some mistakes. I think there was a potential to be on pole today, but Max just did a better job." With celebrity girlfriend Kim Kardashian watching on from the Ferrari garage, Hamilton topped Q1 and Q2 at a circuit where he has four victories, but the Briton could not reproduce his form in Q3. "There's a real fine line with our car where it's over the edge or under the limit and finding that sweet spot is very, very difficult," said seven-times world champion Hamilton. Mercedes driver George Russell, second in the championship, was sixth fastest in Q3 but the Briton is set to start from the back of the grid due to his engine penalty as he looks to bridge the 89-point gap to Antonelli. HADJAR LOSES 100% Q3 RECORD Drivers struggled under braking in the first session, with Esteban Ocon and Lance Stroll both forced to abandon their laps, but the biggest casualty of Q1 was Verstappen's team mate Isack Hadjar. The Frenchman complained about an issue with his gearbox before the 22-year-old returned to the garage without setting a lap time, losing his 100% record of qualifying for Q3 this year. "Nothing Isack could have done. We had a gearbox issue on his car," Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies told Sky Sports. Verstappen also complained about gearbox issues despite advancing from Q2. "Insanely, insanely bad shifts," he said. "The downshifts are so bad." Reigning champion Lando Norris and McLaren team mate Oscar Piastri will line up on the third row after the stewards took no further action following the collision between the two drivers in the sprint. Alpine's Pierre Gasly will start seventh on the grid followed by the Racing Bulls of Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad, and Audi's Nico Hulkenberg completed the top 10.

item.title: Autoridad saudita reporta varios heridos por explosión en aeropuerto de Riad
item.description: Varias personas resultaron heridas en un ataque perpetrado el sábado contra el Aeropuerto Internacional Rey Khalid, en Riad, la capital de Arabia Saudita, lo que obligó a suspender las operaciones, informó la autoridad de aviación civil del país.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari, Enas Alashray
item.content:encoded: Varias personas resultaron heridas en un ataque perpetrado el sábado contra el Aeropuerto Internacional Rey Khalid, en Riad, la capital de Arabia Saudita, lo que obligó a suspender las operaciones, informó la autoridad de aviación civil del país. Nadie ha reivindicado de momento la autoría del ataque, pero ocurre en el contexto de una escalada de ataques con misiles contra el reino por parte de los hutíes yemeníes, alineados con Irán, y sigue a otros esta semana contra el aeropuerto de Riad, en los que murieron cuatro personas, varias resultaron heridas y se dañó un avión. El sistema de alerta temprana de Arabia Saudita no emitió ninguna alerta antes del incidente del sábado. La oficina de prensa del Gobierno saudita no respondió de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios. Uno de los testigos presenciales dijo haber visto una explosión y, a continuación, varias personas heridas tendidas en el suelo dentro del aeropuerto. Más de una decena de ambulancias se dirigieron a toda prisa hacia el aeropuerto. Un viajero herido contó a Reuters que vio algo volando por el cielo fuera del aeropuerto antes de que se derrumbara parte del techo cerca de una puerta de embarque. Tras el ataque, se le preguntó al presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, si Estados Unidos tenía previsto sumarse a los ataques sauditas contra los hutíes. "Es posible. Lo vamos a estudiar. Acabamos de enterarnos del reciente ataque, así que tomaremos una decisión. Actuamos con gran rapidez", dijo. La página web de seguimiento de vuelos flightradar24 mostraba que todos los vuelos con destino a Riad habían sido desviados o cancelados, y que, en un momento dado, solo un helicóptero sobrevolaba el aeropuerto.

item.title: Arteta's Arsenal survive scare to see off feisty Leeds
item.description: Mikel Arteta's Arsenal were staring down the barrel of a second straight Premier League defeat when they fell behind to Leeds United at home on Saturday, but tactical tweaks and inspired substitutions helped them bounce back to claim a 2-1 victory.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Mikel Arteta's Arsenal were staring down the barrel of a second straight Premier League defeat when they fell behind to Leeds United at home on Saturday, but tactical tweaks and inspired substitutions helped them bounce back to claim a 2-1 victory. After frustrating the champions during the opening 45 minutes with stifling defending, Leeds took the lead through James Justin 10 minutes after the break, but Riccardo Calafiori equalised for Arteta's side before substitute Bruno Guimaraes grabbed the winner in the 70th minute. "They are extremely well-organised, they are very physical, they are committed in everything that they do," Arteta told TNT Sports. Arsenal's last game before the lengthy international window ended in an embarrassing 3-0 defeat by Brighton & Hove Albion, and it looked like they might be frustrated again as their attacking play stuttered. "When you don't finish the actions, and we hit some great areas in the first half to have much more end product than we did, and we lost the ball just before the last action, and when that happens and they had moments to run, they are a threat," Arteta explained. "We keep fouling them, we give them throw-ins and restarts and set pieces. They are incredible the way they attack, the belief and the conviction they have to attack the box." Leeds came into Saturday's clash unbeaten in the league, but Calafiori's goal seemed to knock the wind out of their sails, and the introduction of Guimaraes in a triple substitution with Jurrien Timber and Viktor Gyokeres in the 63rd minute proved the turning point. "We bring a lot of leadership in those three players - we brought a goal threat, we brought people who can win duels because it was very man-orientated, people that can get away from that, people that can play forward and penetrate. Against this high press, and they did an incredible job," Arteta said. With many of his players on international duty in recent weeks, Arteta has had to wait a long time to banish the memory of the Brighton defeat. "Immediately after a bad result, and through weeks without your players, you just question, 'Okay, how are we going to be?'," he said. "We reacted incredibly well. We really need to enjoy the victory, because we are realising how this Premier League is going to pan out."

item.title: Abbas aplaza las elecciones palestinas y fija las presidenciales para septiembre de 2027
item.description: El presidente palestino, Mahmud Abás, aplazó el sábado las elecciones legislativas previstas para el próximo mes hasta el 11 de septiembre de 2027 y convocó unas elecciones presidenciales para esa misma fecha, achacando el retraso a Israel y a la situación de seguridad en los territorios palestinos.
item.dc:creator: Ali Sawafta, Nidal Al-Mughrabi, Eman Abouhassira
item.content:encoded: El presidente palestino, Mahmud Abás, aplazó el sábado las elecciones legislativas previstas para el próximo mes hasta el 11 de septiembre de 2027 y convocó unas elecciones presidenciales para esa misma fecha, achacando el retraso a Israel y a la situación de seguridad en los territorios palestinos. El decreto de Abbas citaba "los obstáculos que plantean las medidas israelíes" y la necesidad de establecer unas condiciones políticas, de seguridad y sobre el terreno adecuadas para celebrar "elecciones libres, justas e inclusivas", informó la agencia oficial de noticias palestina WAFA. El decreto instaba a los palestinos de Jerusalén, Cisjordania y Gaza a acudir a las urnas. Existían serias dudas sobre si las elecciones de la Autoridad Palestina se celebrarían el próximo mes. Los palestinos no han celebrado elecciones legislativas ni presidenciales desde 2005-2006, tras lo cual el rival de Abbas, el grupo islamista Hamás, tomó el control de Gaza, derrocando a sus partidarios. Abbas ha gobernado por decreto desde que expiró su mandato presidencial en 2009. El decreto señaló que los ataques militares israelíes, la expansión de los asentamientos, la violencia de los colonos y las restricciones de movimiento en Cisjordania, incluido Jerusalén Este, junto con la continua retención por parte de Israel de los ingresos fiscales palestinos, planteaban dificultades para la preparación y celebración de las elecciones de noviembre. En Gaza, el decreto señalaba las "condiciones humanitarias y de seguridad excepcionales", la retirada incompleta de las fuerzas israelíes, la falta de avances en la reconstrucción y el incumplimiento de los acuerdos para el despliegue de fuerzas internacionales de estabilización y de policía. Las restricciones israelíes al acceso del personal de la comisión electoral y de los observadores internacionales a Gaza y Jerusalén Este también complicaron los preparativos, según el decreto. La decisión de aplazar las elecciones se tomó tras consultar con las facciones y fuerzas políticas palestinas. También tenía por objeto dar tiempo para que se lleve a cabo un diálogo nacional palestino exhaustivo con el fin de reforzar la unidad y abordar los retos a los que se enfrenta el proceso electoral. Dos responsables palestinos dijeron el jueves a Reuters que los líderes del movimiento Fatah, de Abbas, y de su rival Hamás habían acordado en una reunión el miércoles en El Cairo aplazar las elecciones. COMPROMISO CON ELECCIONES El aplazamiento se anuncia apenas unas semanas después de que Abbas reafirmó el calendario electoral de noviembre en su discurso del 24 de septiembre ante la Asamblea General de la ONU, en un intento por impulsar reformas respaldadas internacionalmente. Abbas se había comprometido por escrito con el presidente francés Emmanuel Macron y con el príncipe heredero saudí Mohammed bin Salman a celebrar elecciones presidenciales y legislativas como parte del reconocimiento por parte de Francia de un Estado palestino en septiembre de 2025. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores francés dijo el jueves que la celebración de las elecciones era esencial y acogió con satisfacción la puesta en marcha de una misión de observación electoral de la UE.

item.title: Augsburg score fastest Bundesliga goal but Bayern snatch comeback draw
item.description: Augsburg's Robin Fellhauer scored after eight seconds of the game against visitors Bayern Munich on Saturday to record the fastest goal in Bundesliga history, but the German champions twice came from a goal down to snatch a 2-2 draw.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Augsburg's Robin Fellhauer scored after eight seconds of the game against visitors Bayern Munich on Saturday to record the fastest goal in Bundesliga history, but the German champions twice came from a goal down to snatch a 2-2 draw. Fellhauer benefited from a blunder by Bayern's Manuel Neuer as the keeper tried to clear but sent the ball to the Augsburg player who improved the record held jointly by Kevin Volland and Karim Bellarabi with goals after nine seconds. The Bavarians, whose only league defeat in their last 48 matches was by Augsburg in January, upped their game after the break, having an effort ruled offside in the 51st before Ismael Saibari bagged the equaliser four minutes later. It was another Neuer error that put Augsburg ahead again in the 64th minute, the 40-year-old punching Calvin Brackelmann's shot into the path of Rodrigo Ribeiro who only had to push the ball over the line. Bayern battled back once more, however, when Harry Kane, who hit the woodwork in the first half, cut the ball back for Nathaniel Brown to tap in the equaliser 10 minutes from time. Gnabry hit the post three minutes but Bayern had to settle for a point and second place on 11. Borussia Dortmund are top on 13 points.

item.title: Three injured in Poland's third youth stabbing attack in four days
item.description: Three people were injured in a stabbing attack at a further education college in Warsaw on Saturday, police said, the latest in a series of incidents that have stoked concerns in Poland about copycat violence among young people.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Three people were injured in a stabbing attack at a further education college in Warsaw on Saturday, police said, the latest in a series of incidents that have stoked concerns in Poland about copycat violence among young people. On Friday [USN:L1N45V0E9 TEXT:"thousands of police"] visited schools nationwide to try to reassure pupils after two stabbing sprees by teenagers in as many days sparked rumours of potential further attacks, fears that Saturday's incident is likely to intensify. "At 12:30 today, we received a report of an incident involving the use of a dangerous weapon," police spokesperson Jakub Filipiak told Reuters. "One person was injured and transported to the hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. Two other bystanders also sustained injuries but did not require hospitalisation." He said the attacker was a 21-year-old student of the college. State news agency PAP reported that the victims were two 17-year-old girls and a 24-year-old woman who had come to submit enrollment documents. Preliminary police findings indicated that the attacker and victims did not know one other, PAP reported. Police said on Saturday they had inspected some 50,000 facilities since Friday and detained 76 people. Authorities had previously said most of the people detained were teenagers who had made threats online. On Thursday, a 15-year-old former pupil wearing a helmet-mounted camera [USN:L8N45U0GO TEXT:"killed a caretaker"] and injured two teachers at a primary school in Leszczydol-Nowiny, northeast of Warsaw. On Wednesday, a 19-year-old [USN:L1N45T0N9 TEXT:"wounded 10 people"] including himself at a school in Ostroleka, north of the capital.

item.title: Rayo-Athletic match abandoned after fans protest against club owner
item.description: The LaLiga match between Rayo Vallecano and Athletic Club was abandoned on Saturday after home fans lobbed paper airplanes and small rubber balls onto the pitch in protest against the Madrid club's owner midway through the first half.
item.dc:creator: David Latona
item.content:encoded: The LaLiga match between Rayo Vallecano and Athletic Club was abandoned on Saturday after home fans lobbed paper airplanes and small rubber balls onto the pitch in protest against the Madrid club's owner midway through the first half. The game was the first of this league season played at the Estadio de Vallecas, which was temporarily [USN:L1N43U0P3 TEXT:"closed"] after an audit found serious safety issues. Rayo fans blame negligence by club owner Raul Martin Presa, who in turn accused regional authorities of deliberately targeting his club. The Sports Association of Rayo Vallecano fan group said in a statement after the suspension that their protest was "legitimate and democratic... necessary and peaceful." It added that it was the "consequence of three decades of putting the safety and health of 15,000 people at risk every fortnight". La Liga said in a statement on social media it "strongly condemned this type of behaviour, which endangers safety and makes the normal development of the competition impossible". A new date and time for the match will be announced shortly, LaLiga said. Athletic returned to Bilbao, saying on social media that LaLiga had communicated the game would not take place later on Saturday or on Sunday. Last season's Conference League finalists Rayo released a statement saying the club would seek to identify and discipline those responsible, adding that the forced postponement was part of a sustained campaign of disruption by the fan group. The players, officials and supporters present were "victims of an attack on their rights and freedoms, committed by an organised group of intolerant individuals," said the statement. "UNSUSTAINABLE SITUATION" Rayo captain Oscar Valentin said on social media that "an unsustainable situation had reached its limit" and too little had been done to prevent things getting to this point. "It is necessary to listen to and understand the discontent of our fans. We need a way of bringing ALL parties closer together, always putting the common good first and, above all, the good of Rayo Vallecano," Valentin added. After Rayo's first three home games were moved to the stadium of second-tier Leganes, registering some of La Liga's lowest-ever attendance figures, home fans started chanting, jeering and whistling against Presa before kickoff on Saturday. By the 13th minute - when Rayo ultras usually chant the song "Presa leave already" - hundreds of fans launched paper planes and small rubber balls onto the pitch, prompting the referee to suspend play. A 15-minute pause ensued, during which the stadium's speaker urged spectators not to throw objects onto the field as staff hastily removed them. When play resumed a little later, fans in the south stand again hurled objects onto the pitch and the referee abandoned the game. Anger at Presa's management has [USN:L8N3NH005 TEXT:"reached a peak"] in recent months, following the closure of Vallecas Stadium for Rayo's opening home games of the season. In a friendly against Cagliari last Saturday, anti-Presa graffiti appeared in the VIP box, which fans surrounded in protest before leaving the stadium.

item.title: Several wounded in Riyadh airport attack, operations suspended, Saudi aviation authority says
item.description: Several people were wounded in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh on Saturday that forced a suspension of operations, the country's civil aviation authority said.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari, Enas Alashray
item.content:encoded: Several people were wounded in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh on Saturday that forced a suspension of operations, the country's civil aviation authority said. There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack, but it comes amid an escalation of [USN:L1N45V08F TEXT:"missile strikes"] by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis against Saudi Arabia. The airport had already been struck in two earlier attacks this week that left four people dead and exposed vulnerabilities in the kingdom's ability to defend itself as it wages war on the Houthis. Saudi Arabia's early warning system did not issue an alert ahead of Saturday's incident. The Saudi government's media office did not immediately respond to questions from Reuters. One eyewitness at the airport on Saturday reported seeing an explosion and then multiple people lying injured on the ground inside. More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing towards the facility. An injured traveller told Reuters they saw something fly across the sky outside the airport before part of the ceiling near a departure gate collapsed. US TO "LOOK AT" JOINING SAUDI FIGHT AGAINST HOUTHIS: TRUMP Following the attack, US President Donald Trump, speaking to reporters outside the White House, was asked whether the United States planned to join Saudi strikes on the Houthis. "We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack, so we'll make a decision. We move very quickly," he said. The US embassy in Riyadh said it was "aware of attacks" and "strongly recommends all US citizens avoid this airport and surrounding areas." The UK and Irish embassies in Saudi Arabia said in statements on X that they were also aware of a "serious incident" at the airport. The Canadian embassy said that "ongoing military activity" had impacted operations at the airport. RIYADH DUE TO HOLD MAJOR SUMMITS Flight-tracking site flightradar24 showed all flights to Riyadh had either been diverted or cancelled, with only a helicopter hovering over the airport at one point. Kuwait Airways said it had cancelled flights to and from the Saudi capital due to what it described as the closure of Riyadh airport because of the "security situation" there. Etihad Airways and Qatar Airways earlier cancelled multiple flights between their respective hubs and Riyadh, with some cancellations extending into Monday. Houthi attacks on Thursday and earlier in the week had already prompted a number of carriers to suspend or cancel services to the Saudi capital, shortly before Riyadh is due to host [USN:L8N45W01K TEXT:"major energy and investment conferences"]. Organisers of those conferences said on Saturday they would go ahead as planned, and they sought to reassure attendees of their security. The Houthis have said airliners should avoid Saudi airspace, declaring it a zone of military operations after the Saudi-backed Yemeni government launched an offensive against the group earlier this month.

item.title: Ronaldo, provisionalmente suspendido por abandono de la selección portuguesa, según medios
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo ha sido suspendido provisionalmente por la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol (FPF) tras la apertura de un expediente disciplinario por la marcha del delantero de la concentración de la selección nacional, informaron el sábado medios de comunicación portugueses.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cristiano Ronaldo ha sido suspendido provisionalmente por la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol (FPF) tras la apertura de un expediente disciplinario por la marcha del delantero de la concentración de la selección nacional, informaron el sábado medios de comunicación portugueses. El jugador, de 41 años, abandonó la concentración del equipo en Copenhague antes del partido de la Liga de Naciones que Portugal disputó contra Dinamarca la semana pasada, tras una desavenencia con el seleccionador Jorge Jesús. Ronaldo, que no llegó a salir al campo en el partido contra Noruega, acusó a Jesús de haber incumplido en dos ocasiones su palabra respecto a su papel en el equipo. Según el periódico portugués A Bola, la FPF confirmó que se había abierto un expediente disciplinario. "Sin perjuicio de la suspensión preventiva automática a la que estaba sujeto hasta la fecha de inicio del procedimiento, se dictó una suspensión preventiva no automática del jugador y se concedió carácter de urgencia al procedimiento", dijo la FPF, según el medio. Ronaldo se disculpó el martes por no haber saludado a la afición tras el partido contra Noruega y por haber abandonado a sus compañeros de equipo, y añadió que seguiría estando disponible tras cumplir cualquier sanción derivada del incidente. Reuters se puso en contacto con la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol para recabar sus comentarios.

item.title: UN Human Rights office condemns racist abuse targeting Gauff
item.description: The United Nations Human Rights office has condemned online racist abuse faced by Coco Gauff after a replayed point sparked a backlash against the American tennis player this week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United Nations Human Rights office has condemned online racist abuse faced by Coco Gauff after a replayed point [USN:L4N45S06O TEXT:"sparked a backlash"] against the American tennis player this week. Gauff was targeted after stopping play during a crucial point in her win over Sun Xinran at the China Open, raising her hand to complain about a flickering advertising board as Sun was about to hit a winner. The umpire ordered the point to be replayed after a video review, and Gauff went on to win the match 7-5 6-1, but the American later revealed in a social media post that she had received a huge amount of racist abuse following the match. "You can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist," Gauff, who is Black, said on X in reply to a post containing a racial slur. The official UN Human Rights office posted a statement on Saturday calling for players, coaches and sports bodies to unite against racial and sexist abuse. "Racist messages such as those targeting tennis player Coco Gauff online are appalling and illustrate that Black female athletes are specifically targeted for vitriol and racial abuse," it wrote on X. "There is no place in sport for racial or sexist slurs and abuse. Players, coaches, and sports bodies need to stand up for those facing such attacks and fans need to push back against those who sully sport with racism and sexism." Reuters has contacted the WTA, the governing body of women's tennis, and tournament organisers in Beijing for comment. Twice Grand Slam winner Gauff [USN:L1N45T0DY TEXT:"exited the tournament"] on Wednesday with a round-of-16 loss, and said the incident had left her drained. A study by the WTA and World Tennis showed players were subjected to over 12,000 abusive posts and messages on social media in 2025, up from 8,000 posts the previous year.

item.title: Ronaldo provisionally suspended after national team walkout, media reports say
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after disciplinary proceedings were opened over the forward's departure from the national team camp, Portuguese media reported on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after disciplinary proceedings were opened over the forward's departure from the national team camp, Portuguese media reported on Saturday. The 41-year-old left the squad's base in [USN:L6N45M17Z TEXT:"Copenhagen"] before Portugal's Nations League match against Denmark last week, after a rift with head coach Jorge Jesus. Ronaldo, an unused substitute against Norway, [USN:L6N45M17Z TEXT:"accused Jesus"] of twice breaking his word regarding his role in the team. After Portugal's 2-1 win, Jesus denied he had made any agreement with the player but left the door open for his return. According to Portuguese newspaper A Bola, the FPF confirmed that disciplinary proceedings had been opened against Ronaldo. "Without prejudice to the automatic preventive suspension to which he was subject until the date of initiation, a non-automatic preventive suspension of the player was determined, and the proceedings were given urgent status," the federation was quoted as saying. FPF president Pedro Proenca said everyone within the federation wanted Ronaldo to return to the national team once the matter was resolved. "The Portuguese Football Federation and its president, in this spirit of tranquility, speaking with all parties, who have already publicly demonstrated their desire to have the captain back with us, there is an expressed wish from everyone," he was quoted as saying by A Bola. "This includes the federation, the FPF president, the national team coach, the captain and the players." Regarding Ronaldo's disciplinary process, Proenca added: "That will depend solely on the Disciplinary Committee, which is an autonomous body, and it will do its job." Ronaldo apologised on Tuesday for failing to acknowledge supporters after the Norway game and for leaving his teammates, adding that he would remain available for selection after serving any punishment arising from the incident.

item.title: Guimaraes grabs winner as Arsenal rally to beat Leeds
item.description: Arsenal came back from a goal down to beat Leeds United 2-1 at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, with Brazilian Bruno Guimaraes coming off the bench to net the winner as the Premier League resumed following a lengthy international break.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Arsenal came back from a goal down to beat Leeds United 2-1 at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, with Brazilian Bruno Guimaraes coming off the bench to net the winner as the Premier League resumed following a lengthy international break. The competition returned under a cloud, with Manchester City found guilty by an independent commission of more than 100 breaches of the [USN:L6N45L10G TEXT:"league's financial rules"] over nine years and their failure to co-operate with the investigation. City have denied wrongdoing and have appealed against the decision. On the pitch, champions Arsenal climbed to second in the table on 15 points, behind City on goal difference before the Manchester club travel to Liverpool on Sunday. Chelsea struck twice in the opening three minutes en route to a 5-1 thrashing of Bournemouth, with Jordan Henderson and Joao Pedro bagging two goals apiece, and are fifth on 10 points. Tottenham Hotspur struck in stoppage time to salvage a 1-1 draw at Manchester United as both sides' struggles continued. Brighton & Hove Albion climbed to third, two points off top spot, with a 2-0 win at Sunderland. Aston Villa and visiting Brentford drew 2-2, while Ipswich Town edged Fulham 2-1 at Portman Road with a last-gasp goal to leave the last-placed London side without a league victory this season. FRUSTRATING FIRST HALF Arsenal were looking to bounce back, having slumped to a 3-0 defeat at Brighton in the last game before the break but endured a frustrating first half as they struggled to create chances. Their play improved in the second period, but Leeds took the lead in the 55th minute when James Justin slammed home a clever pull-back from Gabriel Gudmundsson. Riccardo Calafiori levelled for Arsenal seven minutes later, the Italian jumping to steer home Ben White's knock-down and, sensing his side could grab all three points, manager Mikel Arteta rang the changes. He sent on Guimaraes, Jurrien Timber and Viktor Gyokeres, and was rewarded when Guimaraes grabbed the winner with a brilliantly worked goal in the 70th minute, sending a low shot into the far corner of the net from the edge of the box. "It was such a difficult game, obviously after the international break it's never easy, especially after a defeat in our last game," Calafiori said. "I think we had some tough moments, but I think we deserved the winner. We acted well after the goal we conceded." Leeds are sixth on nine points. UNLIKELY HERO At Stamford Bridge, Henderson was Chelsea's unlikely hero, opening the scoring in the second minute when Cole Palmer, fresh from signing a new contract, drove forward from the halfway line before setting him up to score. Chelsea struck again a minute later when Henderson found Morgan Rogers, whose curling effort deflected in off defender Antonio Silva. Chelsea extended their lead 40 seconds after halftime through Joao Pedro before Evanilson pulled one back for the visitors five minutes later. Joao Pedro netted the Blues' fourth before Henderson capped the win with a superb curling free kick. Henderson, 36, became the oldest player to be directly involved in three-plus Premier League goals since Cristiano Ronaldo in April 2022. At Old Trafford, Spurs were the better team but United punished their wastefulness in the 73rd minute when Matheus Cunha picked out Bryan Mbeumo in the box, and Mbeumo slotted home with United's second shot on target. Rodrigo Bentancur was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw during a 78th-minute melee. But 10-man Spurs equalised in the 92nd minute when Dominic Solanke got away from Lisandro Martinez to nod Sandro Tonali's cross home for a well-deserved leveller that got them off the bottom of the table. They are 18th on three points, while United are 12th with six points. Brighton's Maxim de Cuyper and Jaouen Hadjam scored in the second half for their side, whose victory came despite seeing Pascal Struijk red-carded in the 57th minute. Brentford's Kristoffer Ajer struck in the 79th to salvage a draw at Villa that left his team fourth on 10 points. Yehor Yarmolyuk had opened the scoring for the visitors before Nicolas Jackson and John McGinn replied for Villa. Ipswich captain Dara O'Shea scored in the 92nd minute to snatch victory over Fulham, who led through Ryan Sessegnon until the 88th minute when Abdoul Ouattara fired in a fine equaliser.

item.title: Spanish lawyer Gonzalez Durantez launches centrist party for November election
item.description: Lawyer Miriam Gonzalez Durantez launched a new Spanish political party on Saturday to run in an early general election on November 29, promising to rise above a growing ideological divide, recover democratic values and depoliticise institutions.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lawyer Miriam Gonzalez Durantez launched a new Spanish political party on Saturday to run in an [USN:L1N45V07B TEXT:"early general election"] on November 29, promising to rise above a growing ideological divide, recover democratic values and depoliticise institutions. Gonzalez Durantez, who is married to former British Deputy Prime Minister Nick Clegg and specialises in international and EU trade law, said the party, called Democracy21, will run in the election in Madrid and Barcelona. The party enters a volatile political landscape after Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called the snap election on Monday following parliament's rejection of measures to address a [USN:L8N45Q06Q TEXT:"mounting housing crisis"]. Opinion polls point to the conservative People's Party (PP) and far-right Vox likely winning a combined parliamentary majority. Referring to the left-right political divide in Spain exemplified by the deep rivalry between the Socialists and the PP, she criticised "two rigid blocs with nothing to foster consensus". Gonzalez Durantez called on Spaniards to "set aside our ideological differences, to stand united, and to work together to safeguard democracy and modernise the country." The crisis has triggered continuing mass protests over home shortages and surging rents, stoked by the eviction of an 87-year-old woman, whose death on Tuesday further angered protesters. Gonzalez Durantez blamed both the ruling coalition and the opposition, which controls most of Spain's regions, for the housing crisis, calling their politicians "a cost, a burden for the country" who expressly failed to develop and urbanise the land. "They haven't used the permits to build housing; instead, they've used them to line the coffers of their city councils. They've imposed so many regulations, many of them absurd, that they've doubled the price per square meter of construction and have made it almost impossible for us to build affordable housing," she told supporters. Central government can set housing legislation and devise nationwide plans for incentives and subsidies, but their implementation, and wider urban planning, is largely devolved to regional governments and municipalities. She said she would identify a problem and not play politics with it. "I won’t use it to pit one group against another, no, I’ll simply fix it."

item.title: Home favourite Zheng sets up China Open final against Andreeva
item.description: French Open winner Mirra Andreeva will face Olympic champion and home favourite Zheng Qinwen in the China Open final after the Russian fourth seed eased past Nikola Bartunkova and unseeded Zheng overpowered Elise Mertens in Saturday's semi-finals.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: French Open winner Mirra Andreeva will face Olympic champion and home favourite Zheng Qinwen in the China Open final after the Russian fourth seed eased past Nikola Bartunkova and unseeded Zheng overpowered Elise Mertens in Saturday's semi-finals. Zheng, who received a wildcard entry to the tournament after recovering from an elbow injury, became the first Chinese player to reach the final in Beijing as she outplayed Belgian 13th seed Mertens 7-5 6-2 after Andreeva crushed Bartunkova 6-2 6-2. Zheng made an early break to build a 4-2 lead, but made a number of errors to hand Mertens the break back. But the 24-year-old, who is chasing her first WTA 1000 title on home soil, remained calm to build a 6-5 lead, before her strong crosscourt forehand earned her another break point which she converted when Mertens netted. Zheng dominated the second set to secure her second clash with Andreeva, having beaten the Russian when they met in the 2024 Beijing quarter-finals. "I always want to give my best here. It's like the fifth Grand Slam for me," said Zheng, who reached the semi-final in 2024. In the first semi-final, Andreeva took an hour and 14 minutes to beat Bartunkova and reach her second WTA 1000 final of the year. Czech Bartunkova committed 20 unforced errors, twice as many as Andreeva, as the world number five hit 27 winners to clinch victory. Andreeva is relishing her first China Open final. "Of course, we all know that (Zheng) is playing at home. That's okay. Also, she's been coming back, she's been playing better, she's been beating a lot of great players," the 19-year-old told reporters.

item.title: Neither Putin nor Trump wanted to hang up first, Kremlin aide says after 'very friendly' call
item.description: A conversation on Friday between President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump was "very substantive and friendly" and neither leader wanted to be the first to end the call, Russian news agency Interfax quoted a Kremlin aide as saying.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A conversation on Friday between President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump was "very substantive and friendly" and neither leader wanted to be the first to end the call, Russian news agency Interfax quoted a Kremlin aide as saying. During the call, the presidents agreed that Russia would [USN:FWN45V0WZ TEXT:"supply diesel"] to the US and global markets to lower fuel prices, prompting an unexpected temporary easing of US sanctions on Russian fuel that has [USN:L1N45V0WX TEXT:"dismayed"] Ukraine. The Kremlin said most of the conversation focused on efforts to resolve the war in Ukraine . Putin also [USN:L1N45V0ZL TEXT:"downplayed"] the likelihood of three-way peace talks resuming soon. Interfax cited Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov on Saturday as saying the conversation lasted an hour and a half. "Neither wanted to be the first to hang up," he said. "They hung up simultaneously, literally at the same time." Kyiv is relying on US support in negotiations to end the war. After news of the call broke on Friday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy [USN:L1N45V0WX TEXT:"condemned"] the diesel deal in unusually blunt terms, calling it a "weak decision" and "an investment in a war that must be ended." The West imposed sanctions, including restrictions on Russian energy imports, after Moscow launched the full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022. Efforts to end the fighting have so far stalled, partly over Russia’s demand for four Ukrainian regions it does not fully control. On Friday, negotiators from the US, Ukraine and European countries [USN:L1N45V11A TEXT:"held talks"] in Miami aimed at reaching agreement on a unified peace proposal in the coming weeks that could be presented to Russia, according to a person familiar with the discussions.

item.title: Palmer firma un contrato con el Chelsea hasta 2034
item.description: El centrocampista ofensivo del Chelsea, Cole Palmer, firmó una ampliación de contrato que le mantendrá en Stamford Bridge hasta 2034, anuncio el sábado el club de la Premier League.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El centrocampista ofensivo del Chelsea, Cole Palmer, firmó una ampliación de contrato que le mantendrá en Stamford Bridge hasta 2034, anuncio el sábado el club de la Premier League. El internacional inglés, de 24 años, se ha convertido en una figura clave desde que llegó al Chelsea procedente del Manchester City en 2023, con un registro de 91 goles en 138 partidos en todas las competiciones. Formó parte de la plantilla que ganó el Mundial de Clubes y la UEFA Conference League. "Hablé con los propietarios, con los directores deportivos y, por supuesto, con el entrenador, y me transmitieron mucha confianza, así que lo lógico era firmar", dijo Palmer. "Al hablar también con los jugadores, veo que todos comparten las mismas ambiciones. Tengo la sensación de que aquí ganaremos grandes títulos constantemente". El Chelsea ha acordado contratos a largo plazo con varios jugadores del primer equipo y con jóvenes promesas. El delantero João Pedro firmó recientemente un contrato hasta 2034, y el extremo Pedro Neto acordó el mes pasado un contrato de seis años.

item.title: La presidencia irlandesa de la UE quiere un recorte del 8% al proyecto de presupuesto para 2028-2034
item.description: La presidencia irlandesa de la Unión Europea (UE) propuso el sábado un recorte del 8% al proyecto de presupuesto de la Comisión Europea para el periodo 2028-2034, a 1,6 billones de euros (1,79 billones de dólares), lo que ha suscitado críticas por parte de los Estados miembros más austeros, que consideran que la reducción no es suficiente.
item.dc:creator: Jan Strupczewski, Yun Chee Foo
item.content:encoded: La presidencia irlandesa de la Unión Europea (UE) propuso el sábado un recorte del 8% al proyecto de presupuesto de la Comisión Europea para el periodo 2028-2034, a 1,6 billones de euros (1,79 billones de dólares), lo que ha suscitado críticas por parte de los Estados miembros más austeros, que consideran que la reducción no es suficiente. La propuesta irlandesa supone, a pesar de todo, un aumento del 30% respecto del presupuesto actual del bloque, que abarca el periodo de 2021 a 2027. El presupuesto de la UE es la principal fuente de financiación de todas las políticas fundamentales del bloque de 27 países. La Comisión, el órgano ejecutivo de la UE, ha señalado que el bloque debe destinar más fondos a la defensa y al impulso de la competitividad europea, mientras que algunos Estados miembros desean mantener la mayor parte del gasto destinado al apoyo a la agricultura y al desarrollo regional. "La 'caja de negociación' supone un ahorro del 8%, es decir, 141.000 millones de euros, respecto a la propuesta original de la Comisión", dijo Irlanda, que actualmente y por seis meses preside la UE, refiriéndose a su propuesta de compromiso. Irlanda ajustó la cifra original de la Comisión, de 2 billones de euros, teniendo en cuenta la inflación en siete años, situándola en 1,76 billones de euros a precios de 2025, lo que supuso una reducción del 8%. "Tal y como lo vemos, el marco de negociación sirve para salvar las numerosas diferencias entre los Estados miembros", dijo el ministro irlandés Thomas Byrne en una rueda de prensa. "Nos acerca a la resolución del trilema presupuestario, abordando las conversaciones sobre la mejor forma de financiar nuevas prioridades en materia de competitividad, investigación, innovación, seguridad y defensa, al tiempo que se abordan las políticas fundamentales", añadió. La propuesta establece un recorte del 3% del gasto en desarrollo regional, agricultura y pesca respecto de las propias cifras de la Comisión —la partida más importante del presupuesto— y una reducción del 13% en el gasto en competitividad y seguridad. Los líderes de la UE debatirán la propuesta irlandesa en Bruselas el 15 y 16 de octubre. El presupuesto de la UE, conocido como Marco Financiero Plurianual, debe ser aprobado por los 27 Estados miembros. (1 dólar = 0,8928 euros)

item.title: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
item.description: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections due next month until September 11, 2027, and called a presidential poll for the same date, blaming Israel and the security situation in the Palestinian territories for the delay.
item.dc:creator: Ali Sawafta, Nidal Al-Mughrabi, Eman Abouhassira
item.content:encoded: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections due next month until September 11, 2027, and called a presidential poll for the same date, blaming Israel and the security situation in the Palestinian territories for the delay. Abbas' decree cited "obstacles posed by Israeli measures" and the need to establish suitable political, security and on-the-ground conditions for "free, fair and inclusive elections", the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported. In a post on X, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar, pointing to the last Palestinian election having been held two decades ago, rejected Abbas' remarks as "yet another ridiculous lie designed to evade responsibility and accountability." There had been serious doubts that the [USN:L8N45G1M5 TEXT:"Palestinian Authority vote"] would go ahead next month. The Palestinians have not held legislative or presidential elections since 2005-2006, after which Abbas' rival, the Islamist group Hamas, seized control of Gaza, ousting his loyalists. Abbas has governed by decree since his presidential mandate expired in 2009. The Palestinian Authority held municipal elections in April in the West Bank and in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza, the only city in the enclave to participate. The vote was the first election held in Gaza since 2006. The decree said Israeli military attacks, settlement expansion, settler violence and movement restrictions in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, along with Israel's continued withholding of Palestinian tax revenues, created challenges to preparing for and holding elections this November. In Gaza , the decree pointed to "exceptional security and humanitarian conditions", the incomplete withdrawal of Israeli forces, the lack of progress in reconstruction and the failure to implement arrangements for deploying international stabilisation forces and police. The decree called on Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza to vote. Israeli restrictions on access for election commission staff and international observers to Gaza and East Jerusalem also complicated preparations, the decree said. Israel typically bans the Palestinian Authority from holding elections in East Jerusalem, territory it captured in the 1967 war and later annexed in a move most countries do not recognize. The decision to postpone followed consultations with Palestinian factions and political forces. It also aimed to allow time for a comprehensive Palestinian national dialogue to strengthen unity and address challenges facing the electoral process. PLEDGE TO HOLD VOTE AFTER TWO DECADES Two Palestinian officials told Reuters on Thursday that leaders of Abbas' Fatah movement and rival Hamas had agreed at a meeting in Cairo on Wednesday to postpone the elections. An August poll by the West Bank-based Palestinian Center for Policy and Survey Research (PSR) showed declining support for both Hamas and Fatah, which many Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank blame for their continuing political divisions. The delay comes just weeks after Abbas reaffirmed the November election timetable in his September 24 address to the UN General Assembly, as he sought to advance internationally backed reforms. Abbas had committed in writing to French President Emmanuel Macron and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to hold presidential and legislative elections as part of France's recognition of a Palestinian state in September 2025. France's foreign ministry [USN:L1N45V090 TEXT:"said on Thursday"] that holding the elections was essential, and it welcomed the launch of an EU election observation mission.

item.title: Report à 2027 des élections palestiniennes
item.description: Le président palestinien Mahmoud Abbas a annulé samedi les élections législatives prévues en novembre en raison de la dégradation de la situation dans les territoires palestiniens et fixé au 11 septembre 2027 la tenue simultanée des élections présidentielle et législatives, a rapporté l'agence de presse officielle palestinienne WAFA.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le président palestinien Mahmoud Abbas a annulé samedi les élections législatives prévues en novembre en raison de la dégradation de la situation dans les territoires palestiniens et fixé au 11 septembre 2027 la tenue simultanée des élections présidentielle et législatives, a rapporté l'agence de presse officielle palestinienne WAFA. Le décret de Mahmoud Abbas évoque les "obstacles créés par les mesures israéliennes" à la tenue des élections en novembre ainsi que la nécessité de réunir des conditions politiques, sécuritaires et de terrain adaptées à l'organisation d'"élections libres, équitables et inclusives". Il appelle les Palestiniens de Jérusalem, de Cisjordanie et de Gaza à participer au scrutin. De sérieux doutes existaient quant à la tenue du scrutin de l'Autorité palestinienne à la fin novembre. Les Palestiniens n'ont plus organisé d'élections législatives ni présidentielle depuis 2005-2006, à l'issue desquelles le Hamas, rival islamiste du président palestinien Mahmoud Abbas, a pris le contrôle de Gaza en évinçant ses partisans. Le décret précise que les attaques militaires israéliennes, l'expansion des colonies, les violences de colons et les restrictions de circulation en Cisjordanie, y compris à Jérusalem-Est, ainsi que la poursuite du gel par Israël des recettes fiscales palestiniennes, ont créé des difficultés pour préparer et organiser les élections à la date initialement prévue. À Gaza, le décret fait état de "conditions sécuritaires et humanitaires exceptionnelles", du retrait inachevé des forces israéliennes, de l'absence de progrès dans la reconstruction et de la non-mise en oeuvre des dispositions relatives au déploiement de forces internationales de stabilisation et de police. Les restrictions imposées par Israël à l'accès de Gaza et de Jérusalem-Est pour les personnels de la commission électorale et les observateurs internationaux ont également compliqué les préparatifs, ajoute le décret. La décision de report fait suite à une résolution du comité exécutif de l'Organisation de libération de la Palestine (OLP) et à des consultations avec les factions palestiniennes et les forces politiques. Elle vise également à laisser le temps nécessaire à un dialogue national palestinien global afin de renforcer l'unité et de répondre aux défis auxquels est confronté le processus électoral.

item.title: Eritrea asks UN to intervene in standoff with Ethiopia
item.description: Eritrea asked the UN Security Council on Saturday to take deterrent measures against Ethiopia, according to a letter seen by Reuters, saying Addis Ababa's accusations of an invasion by Eritrean forces amounted to a "declaration of war".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Eritrea asked the UN Security Council on Saturday to take deterrent measures against Ethiopia, according to a letter seen by Reuters, saying Addis Ababa's accusations of an invasion by Eritrean forces amounted to a "declaration of war". The [USN:L6N45T121 TEXT:"incursion by Eritrean troops"], which [USN:L8N45Q06L TEXT:"Asmara has denied"] and Reuters could not independently verify, has raised fears of a return to [USN:L6N45M0WY TEXT:"all-out war"] along Ethiopia's northern border where the two Horn of Africa neighbours have clashed before. Conflicts elsewhere in the region and tensions across the Red Sea have further raised the stakes. Eritrean Foreign Minister Osman Saleh said in the letter that the incursion claims were part of an Ethiopian plan to justify a war of aggression. He urged the UN to intervene. "Eritrea requests the UN Security Council to forcefully condemn Ethiopia's deplorable declaration of war against Eritrea ... and take the requisite deterrent measures against it in accordance with Chapter VII of the UN Charter," he wrote. Chapter VII allows for measures ranging from sanctions to military action, though Osman did not specify what measures Eritrea was calling for. Ethiopia itself [USN:L8N45V0CC TEXT:"wrote to Security Council members"] on Friday, stating that Eritrean troops had advanced up to 60 km (37 miles) inside the northern region of Tigray in recent days. It warned that the presence of foreign troops left Addis Ababa with no option but to defend itself. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Saturday. ETHIOPIAN TROOPS, MILITIA ALLIES MOVE INTO TIGRAYAN CITY Earlier in the day, Ethiopian government forces and their militia allies entered the Tigrayan city of Adigrat, near the border with Eritrea, three residents said, days after Eritrean troops [USN:L6N45U0QF TEXT:"were "][USN:L6N45U0QF TEXT:"pushed back"] from the strategic city. A video shared on social media and verified by Reuters showed members of a militia allied with the Ethiopian government walking in the streets of Adigrat, which is located 30 km (19 miles) from the border with Eritrea. Three Adigrat residents also told Reuters they had seen the Ethiopian army and an allied militia in the city on Saturday morning, with one of the residents saying they saw soldiers on patrol along with military vehicles. Explosions were reported on Wednesday and Thursday near Adigrat, as the US-based conflict monitor ACLED said Ethiopia used drone strikes against Eritrean forces, who then withdrew from positions near the city. The explosions continued on Friday, according to an Adigrat resident, who told Reuters they had heard repeated explosions overnight and into the morning several kilometres outside town. ETHIOPIAN SEA ACCESS A FLASH POINT Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel said on Friday that Eritrea had shown restraint. He said a 2023 statement by landlocked Ethiopia that it would acquire sovereign access to the sea amounted to declaring a war of aggression against his country. Ethiopia had access to a coastline for decades until Eritrea gained independence from Addis Ababa in 1993. Ethiopia argues that restoring sea access is an existential issue but has said it would be restored through peace and dialogue. Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of backing the rebel alliance that has been battling government troops since September 23 in its northern regions of Tigray, Amhara and Afar. Eritrea has denied doing so. After years of war, Eritrea and Ethiopia made peace in a 2018 agreement that earned Ethiopia's Abiy the Nobel Peace Prize. Eritrea fought in support of Ethiopia’s federal government during a 2020-2022 civil war in Tigray, but relations soured again toward the end of that conflict. The fighting that broke out last month has been the biggest escalation of violence since the Tigray war, in which hundreds of thousands died.

item.title: Ukraine-Une attaque russe fait 20 morts à Zaporijjia, passe d'armes Zelensky-Trump
item.description: Vingt personnes, dont trois enfants, ont été tuées samedi lors d'une attaque russe contre la ville de Zaporijjia, dans le sud de l'Ukraine, au lendemain de l'annonce par le président américain Donald Trump d'un accord levant les sanctions sur le diesel russe, un revers majeur pour Kyiv.
item.dc:creator: Sergiy Chalyi, Max Hunder
item.content:encoded: Vingt personnes, dont trois enfants, ont été tuées samedi lors d'une attaque russe contre la ville de Zaporijjia, dans le sud de l'Ukraine, au lendemain de l'annonce par le président américain Donald Trump d'un accord levant les sanctions sur le diesel russe, un revers majeur pour Kyiv. Une fillette de six ans figure parmi les victimes d'une frappe qui a réduit une partie d'un immeuble résidentiel à l'état de gravats. Dix-huit autres personnes ont été blessées dans cette attaque contre Zaporijjia, ville industrielle dont la périphérie se situe à moins de 30 km de la ligne de front. "Aujourd'hui, la Russie a fêté la levée des sanctions sur les exportations de diesel en larguant cinq bombes planantes sur des immeubles résidentiels à Zaporijjia", a déclaré le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky, dans l'une de ses critiques les plus virulentes à ce jour à l'encontre de la Maison blanche. Donald Trump a rétorqué que Volodimir Zelensky "ferait mieux d'arrêter immédiatement" de bombarder les raffineries russes, ajoutant : "Je suggère qu'ils (les Ukrainiens, NDLR) se trouvent un nouveau dirigeant capable de conclure un accord." L'attaque russe de samedi est la dernière en date d'une série de frappes particulièrement meurtrières en Ukraine ces dernières semaines. Près de 80 civils ont été tués lors de frappes russes mercredi et jeudi, dont au moins 30 dans un bombardement contre la ville-garnison de Kramatorsk, dans l'est du pays, et 22 autres dans une attaque de missile contre la ville de Pryluky, située à environ 130 km à l'est de Kyiv. Le gouverneur local, Mykhaïlo Semikine, a déclaré que la Russie avait frappé plusieurs sites simultanément dans les premières heures de samedi. Des secouristes ont progressé à travers les décombres pour extraire vivants d'autres habitants de l'immeuble. Un homme, dont la jambe était coincée sous les gravats, criait de douleur pendant qu'il était dégagé. "D'AUTRES SIGNAUX SONT NÉCESSAIRES" Zaporijjia, qui comptait plus de 700.000 habitants avant la guerre, est régulièrement visée par les bombardements russes, dont l'intensité s'est accrue au cours des derniers mois. "La nuit dernière a constitué une nouvelle confirmation que la Russie considère tout allègement de la pression comme un signal lui permettant soi-disant de continuer à faire la guerre, de continuer à larguer des bombes sur les villes. D'autres signaux sont nécessaires", a déclaré Volodimir Zelensky. Une attaque de missile menée samedi après-midi a également frappé un restaurant à Kyiv, blessant sept personnes. Des drones russes ont survolé la capitale ukrainienne tout au long de la journée dans le cadre d'une nouvelle vague massive de bombardements, la plus importante depuis les premiers jours de la guerre. Le ministère russe de la Défense a déclaré samedi en début se soirée que ses drones avaient frappé plus tôt un centre de traitement de données à Kyiv ainsi qu'un cargo transportant des fournitures militaires vers le port ukrainien d'Odessa. Dans un communiqué, il a ajouté que le site de Kyiv était utilisé par les forces armées ukrainiennes pour collecter, traiter et stocker des renseignements. Reuters n'a pas été en mesure de vérifier ces informations dans l'immédiat. La décision de Donald Trump de lever les sanctions sur les exportations de diesel russe intervient alors que son administration cherche à enrayer la hausse des prix des carburants, qui ont bondi dans le contexte du conflit opposant les États-Unis à l'Iran. Kyiv avait au contraire exhorté Washington à accroître la pression sur la Russie afin de la contraindre à engager de véritables négociations pour mettre fin à la guerre, qui dure depuis quatre ans et demi. L'ACCORD SUR LE DIESEL A PRIS KYIV PAR SURPRISE Donald Trump a en outre critiqué les frappes ukrainiennes contre les raffineries russes, estimant qu'elles avaient contribué à faire grimper les prix mondiaux. Kyiv dit vouloir un arrêt total des attaques visant les infrastructures énergétiques des deux camps, alors que Moscou continue de pilonner le réseau électrique ukrainien. Samedi, plusieurs secteurs de Kyiv et de sa région ont été privés d'électricité, provoquant l'arrêt complet du métro de la capitale pour la deuxième fois de la semaine. Ces dernières frappes sont intervenues après des discussions à Miami entre responsables ukrainiens et européens et négociateurs américains, vendredi, en vue d'élaborer une proposition commune pour mettre fin à la guerre, selon une source proche du dossier. L'agence de presse officielle russe Tass, citant une source, a rapporté samedi que les émissaires américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner pourraient se rendre à Moscou au cours des deux prochaines semaines. Donald Trump a annoncé l'accord sur le diesel alors que les négociations de vendredi étaient en cours, une décision qui, selon Volodimir Zelensky, a pris Kyiv par surprise. Le président russe Vladimir Poutine a déclaré, à l'issue d'un entretien téléphonique avec son homologue américain, qu'une reprise immédiate des pourparlers de paix était peu probable, invoquant les attaques de drones ukrainiens contre Moscou. Par ailleurs, quatre civils ont été tués et cinq autres blessés à la suite d'attaques ukrainiennes contre la région de Louhansk, sous contrôle russe dans l'est de l'Ukraine, a déclaré samedi le gouverneur local installé par Moscou. Reuters n'a pas été en mesure de vérifier cette information de manière indépendante et l'Ukraine n'a pas fait de commentaire dans l'immédiat.

item.title: Norris apologises after collision dashes McLaren sprint hopes
item.description: World champion Lando Norris apologised to his McLaren team after a final-lap collision with team mate Oscar Piastri wrecked their pursuit of a podium finish at a chaotic Singapore Grand Prix sprint on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Rohith Nair
item.content:encoded: World champion Lando Norris apologised to his McLaren team after a final-lap collision with team mate Oscar Piastri wrecked their pursuit of a podium finish at a [USN:L1N45W02M TEXT:"chaotic Singapore Grand Prix sprint"] on Saturday. The McLaren duo were chasing Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, who was struggling with his tyres in the dying stages of the 20-lap sprint, when disaster struck on the final lap. Norris, running fifth behind Piastri in fourth, attempted to overtake his team mate but clipped the Australian's rear tyre with his front wheel, sending both cars spinning and handing Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli fourth place. "Sorry about that. Obviously I didn't want that to happen but I thought I was fully alongside. I just ran out of space at the apex but I was there," Norris said over the team radio. While Norris limped home to eighth place to claim the final point available, Piastri was forced to retire as he became one of nine cars that did not finish - a record number of retirements for a Formula One sprint race. "I'd rather just go back and review it," Norris told Sky Sports. "I apologised to them that one of the cars is out but, like I said, the rest of it we'll go review." Piastri said he had not seen the incident properly to comment but downplayed its significance as they were not in high points scoring positions. "From where I sit, it's for fourth and fifth for a sprint race, so I'm not that bothered either way," Piastri said. "Just obviously it's a lot of work now for the team to get both cars fixed (ahead of qualifying for Sunday's race). Just a shame for the team." 'SIMPLY NOT ACCEPTABLE' Both McLaren drivers were summoned to meet the stewards after the collision but no further action was taken. The FIA said both drivers "contributed to the incident and that neither driver was wholly or predominantly to blame for the collision." McLaren team principal Andrea Stella was not impressed with his drivers, however, adding that scoring just one point was not enough. "Seeing two McLarens making contact like that is simply not acceptable. This is something that we will discuss with our drivers," he said. "We will do it in private. We will reiterate that the team interest is far bigger than any of us. There's no ego, there's no person that is bigger than the interest of the McLaren Formula One team. "I'm sure, like always, this will be conversations that will lead to the team being more united and even stronger." Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the sprint and the Dutchman, who also [USN:L1N45W02M TEXT:"clinched pole for Sunday's race"] , leapfrogged Norris to climb to fifth in the world championship standings.

item.title: EU's Irish presidency wants 8% cut to proposed 2028-2034 budget plan
item.description: The Irish EU presidency proposed on Saturday an 8% cut in the European Commission's budget plan for the period 2028 to 2034 to €1.6 trillion ($1.79 trillion), drawing criticism from more frugal member states that the reduction is not deep enough.
item.dc:creator: Jan Strupczewski, Yun Chee Foo
item.content:encoded: The Irish EU presidency proposed on Saturday an 8% cut in the European Commission's budget plan for the period 2028 to 2034 to €1.6 trillion ($1.79 trillion), drawing criticism from more frugal member states that the reduction is not deep enough. The Irish proposal still marks a 30% increase over the bloc's current budget, which runs from 2021 to 2027. The EU budget is the main source of financing for all of the 27-country bloc's main policies. The Commission, the EU executive, has said the bloc needs to spend more on defence and boosting European competitiveness, while some member states want to retain most of the expenditure to support farming and regional development. "The Negotiating Box provides savings of 8%, or €141 billion, on the Commission's original proposal," said Ireland, current holder of the EU's six-month rotating presidency, referring to its compromise proposal.
